newsitem.title: UK: Cordiant advertises return to profit.
newsitem.headline: Cordiant advertises return to profit.

text.p: Global advertising and marketing services group Cordiant Plc said Thursday it returned to profit last year as it recovered from the traumatic departure of company founders the Saatchi brothers.
Cordiant, formerly known as Saatchi & Saatchi, announced a 1996 pre-tax profit of 41.8 million pounds ($67 million), after a loss of 22.6 million pounds ($36.1 million) year before.

The company, which still owns the Saatchi & Saatchi advertising agency as well as Bates Worldwide, said it was paying its first dividend for seven years. The dividend was 1 pence (1.6 cents) per share.

Chief Executive Bob Seelert said in an interview the group was recovering from the turmoil of 1995 when the Saatchis, who founded the company in the 1970s, departed following a spectacular boardroom battle.
Their exit triggered the departure of a number of other top executives and the loss of several important accounts.
"We're delivering on the promises we made in 1995 and feel that the company is on a solid foundation for the future," said Seelert, an American.
Cordiant raised some $200 million through a rights issue at the end of 1995 and promised at that time to improve its operating margins and revenue performance.

The group is aiming for revenue growth of at least the market average of 6 percent by the end of 1997. It also aims to lift its operating margins from their 1996 level of 6.4 percent to 10 percent by the end of 1998.
Rival British-based advertising group WPP Plc has margins of over 10 percent while those of U.S. firms Interpublic Group of Companies Inc. and Omnicom Group Inc. are higher still.
The 1995 pre-tax loss was largely due to exceptional items and disposals.
